title: Rook and the Wobbly Bridge
markdown:
A little goblin named Rook lived in the Hollowpeak Hills, and he was fond of a tiny kitten. Moonbeams made silver threads in the trees. The air smelled of damp earth and sleepy wildflowers. The kitten was Fluffernutter: fur as white and soft as a brand-new snowdrift, paws that tiptoed as if walking on the quietest whisper.

Rook loved Fluffernutter more than sparkly pebbles by the creek, more than the crunchiest roots, as much as the tallest trees love the biggest moonbeams. One evening the moon climbed high and painted the world in soft hazy light. “Come, Fluffernutter.” Soft as a moth’s wing on a petal. “We shall explore the little silver forest just past Whisperwind Creek.”

His heart fluttered a little. There was a tiny bridge over the creek, twisty shimmering silver vines that twinkled like a necklace of stars. Some older goblins, gruff, wide-shouldered, muttered that it was a bit wobbly, that it swayed too much when the wind played games. Rook knew, in a place as true as the north star, that it was perfectly safe. He wanted to prove it, especially to Fluffernutter, who sometimes looked a little hesitant at new things.

They padded the mossy path, which remembered many goblin boots and did not complain. Trees whispered secrets to each other and did not include Rook, which was fair, as he was busy. Leaves like pages in an old book. Stars like spilled sugar on dark velvet. Soon, the gentle gurgle of Whisperwind Creek, a happy sigh. The little silver bridge glistened. Vines caught the light and sent sparkles dancing. It looked quite beautiful, and also, Rook had to admit, a little like a necklace that had not decided whether to stay on.

A soft puff of wind, no bigger than a sigh from a sleeping badger, tickled Rook’s ears and made the leaves dance. The bridge swayed, just a whisper, a tiny ripple. Rook’s breath hitched. A small insistent paw patted his ankle, then another. Fluffernutter, big curious emerald eyes.

Rook fumbled for his map, old and smudged. Helpful drawings that were not so helpful now. A squiggly line for the creek, and then a drawing of a mountain lantern. A mountain lantern? What good was that beside a little silver bridge? His confidence flickered like a candle in a sudden breeze.

He thought of Catriona Buttercrust, kindest goblin baker in all the Hollowpeak Hills, round like a perfectly risen bun, flour always dusted on his nose, a smile that could melt a grumpy glacier. Catriona always said, with a twinkle, “A little courage, Rook, is like a warm loaf on a chilly morning. It fills you up and makes everything feel better.”

Deep breath. Rook scooped Fluffernutter close. Fur like holding a moonbeam. “It’s alright, little one. We’ll just try one step. Just one brave little step.” One small earth-brown boot onto the silver vines. Cool, slightly rough. Wood creaked, a low groan. Damp moss. The bridge held. Fluffernutter purred, a rumbling happy sound through Rook’s chest.

One step. Then another. The bridge swayed again, and this time it felt like a friendly little dance under the watchful moon. Worries melted like frost. They reached the other side. The forest floor felt solid and welcoming.

Rook looked down. Fluffernutter was batting a dangling moonbeam, tail twitching. A wide goblin smile, slightly crooked teeth. The bridge was safe, just as he had thought. They did not wait for the trees to clap.

They continued their moonlit stroll, steps light and sure. The path home felt welcoming. Warm beds waited, and sweet dreams of silver vines that held. In the morning, perhaps, Catriona would have a bun left over. Rook would mention the bridge. He would not mention the map’s lantern, which had been no help at all, except as a thing to put back in a pocket.
characters: Rook (young goblin), Fluffernutter (kitten), Catriona Buttercrust (goblin baker)
author: StoryGen Community
